notes: Highly effective for anatomical accuracy when used with the 'anatomyfix' trigger word at a scale of 1.0-1.2. Perfect for ballet poses and other complex human figures.
Excellent for full-body shots with specific body type requirements. Best used with the 'slider, bodyweight' trigger word at a scale of 0.5-1.0. Provides consistent, high-quality results.
Designed to enhance detail and sharpness. Works well with close-up portrait prompts at a scale of 0.5. Effect is noticeable but subtle, complementing the base model.
Adds a cinematic, professional photography style. Effect is most noticeable at a scale of 0.65. Does not significantly improve scores over the base zimage model for standard portraits.

Intended for head/face swapping, but the prompt used ('BFS head face swap') is a technical command, not a descriptive prompt. This leads to a fundamental prompt adherence failure. The LoRA itself may be effective with a proper descriptive prompt.

NO skin-realism improvement (artifacts identical 4.5 vs 4.5 baseline-vs-adapter A/B). Raised pixel sharpness (Laplacian 244 vs 231) but VLM read it as noise not pores. Tested in weak regime (9 steps @ 640x960, scale 0.7 model-only; author recs 0.2-0.6 model+clip + >15 steps). NOT a skin lever — see avoid.jsonl plasticky-skin ceiling.
